observation.visible_scene: An open, snow-covered field dotted with low dry bushes under a flat, overcast sky tinted purple. For the first portion of the excerpt a man wearing a dark green hooded jacket, sunglasses and gloves stands roughly centered in the middle ground, facing the camera. After a discontinuity the same static landscape is shown without the man, and then an explosion/impact occurs in the middle distance, producing a rising dust-and-snow plume.
visible_changes: Frames 1-12: the man stands nearly in place with only small posture/head shifts; the camera and background (horizon line, bush positions) remain fixed.
Between frame 12 (t=0.734) and frame 13 (t=0.800) the man is abruptly absent while the background framing is unchanged, indicating an editing cut / discontinuity rather than a continuous exit.
Frames 13-21: the empty snowy field is static; no motion is visible.
Frame 22 (t=1.401): a brief bright flash appears at a point in the middle-distance bushes.

Frames 23-41: at that same location a cloud of dust/snow erupts, then continuously billows upward and outward, growing taller and wider and drifting as a rounded, expanding plume; the plume's base stays at the impact point while its head rises, so the change is expansion/rise of a single cloud, not translation of an object.
Throughout, the foreground bushes and the horizon do not move, confirming a stationary camera; the only real motion is the man's minor sway (pre-cut) and the growing plume (post-cut).
outside_clip_unknowns: What caused the flash and plume (projectile, blast, etc.) is not shown.
What the man did or where he went at the cut is not shown.
Whether the plume dissipates, ignites, or settles after t=2.669 is beyond the excerpt.
uncertain_details: The transition at frame 13 is treated as a likely edit cut because the identical background loses the centered man instantaneously, though an off-camera rapid departure cannot be fully excluded.
The plume's composition (loose snow/dust vs smoke) cannot be determined from color alone.
Minor apparent changes in the man's stance across frames 1-12 may be slight body sway rather than intended movement.

and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.

do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.

properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;

and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
